output_json.patch_notes:
Root cause: the JSONP "callback" request parameter (read via HttpServletRequest.getParameter in AgentServlet and via the hand-rolled ParsedUri query parser in the JVM agent) was concatenated verbatim in front of the JSON payload and written into a text/javascript response with zero validation, at 4 sink call sites (AgentServlet.sendAllJSON, AgentServlet's streaming path via IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose, JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON, and JolokiaHttpHandler's streaming path via the same shared IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose).

Fix: added IoUtil.validateCallback(String) — a shared helper enforcing a strict "safe JS identifier" grammar (letters/digits/_/$, optionally dotted or with numeric array indices; e.g. `foo`, `foo.bar`, `foo[0]`). Any callback value that doesn't match is rejected with IllegalArgumentException.
- IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose now calls validateCallback() before writing anything — this single change protects both the servlet's and the JVM agent's streaming response paths (the sink shared by two of the four traces in the alert).
- AgentServlet.sendAllJSON and JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON each now call validateCallback() before building the wrapped content, as defense-in-depth at their own sink (covers the two non-streaming fallback traces).
- AgentServlet.sendResponse and JolokiaHttpHandler.sendResponse now validate the callback immediately after extracting it, before dispatching to either the streaming or non-streaming path. On an invalid callback they short-circuit to a plain-text 400 response ("Invalid callback given") via new sendBadCallbackError helpers, so the malicious value never reaches a context a browser would execute — this is the primary, earliest interception point and blocks all 4 sinks in both agent flavors for both GET and POST (AgentServlet.doGet/doPost both funnel through the same sendResponse/handle code).

Because ParsedUri.getParameter() (JVM agent) always returns values[0] regardless of whether the callback arrived as a single query param or via the repeated-parameter array-building branch, and because URL-decoding happens before validation runs, this fix transparently covers both traces of vulnerability #3 in the alert and blocks URL-encoded bypass attempts (e.g. %3C for `<`) since validation runs on the fully decoded string.

Added regression tests:
- IoUtilTest: validates the new validateCallback() accepts safe names (plain, dotted, bracketed, null) and rejects script-breakout payloads, parens/quotes, and whitespace; also verifies streamResponseAndClose throws IllegalArgumentException for a malicious callback instead of writing it.
- AgentServletTest: new `withMaliciousCallbackRejected` test drives the full doGet() flow with the `xss</script><script>alert(document.domain)</script>` callback and asserts the servlet responds with a plain "Invalid callback given" body (400) containing no `<script>` markup, mirroring the existing `withCallback` happy-path test's mocking style.
output_json.risk_notes: Behavioral change: requests using a "callback" parameter that is not a valid (optionally dotted/bracketed) JavaScript identifier now receive an HTTP 400 with a plain-text body instead of a 200 JSONP response — this is an intentional, minimal behavior change required to close the XSS, and matches the alert's regression_hint ("must be rejected ... rather than silently substituted or passed through"). Legitimate callback names (plain identifiers, dotted paths like `myApp.jolokia.callback`, or array-indexed like `cb[0]`) are unaffected — verified via existing tests (`withCallback` in AgentServletTest, `testCallbackGet`/`testCallbackPost` in JolokiaHttpHandlerTest) plus new regression tests. Ran the finder's POV before and after: it passed (exit 0) before the patch and now fails (exit 1) because the servlet no longer reflects the payload in an executable response — this is expected and confirms the fix. One pre-existing, unrelated test-environment issue was observed and left untouched: JolokiaHttpHandlerTest has 12 failures on the unpatched baseline too (NullPointerException in `com.sun.net.httpserver.Headers.set` inside the test's own `prepareExchange` helper), caused by a JDK-version mismatch in the container, not by this change — confirmed by reproducing the identical failures via `git stash` on the original code before restoring the patch.
output_json.summary: Fixed CWE-079 JSONP callback reflected-XSS in Jolokia's servlet and JVM-agent HTTP handlers. Added a shared IoUtil.validateCallback() that enforces a strict JS-identifier grammar (^[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*(\.[a-zA-Z_$][a-zA-Z0-9_$]*|\[\d+\])*$) on any "callback" value before it is embedded unescaped into a JSONP response. Wired this validation into all four sink call sites named in the alert: IoUtil.streamResponseAndClose (shared by AgentServlet's and JolokiaHttpHandler's streaming paths), AgentServlet.sendAllJSON, and JolokiaHttpHandler.sendAllJSON. Additionally, both AgentServlet.sendResponse and JolokiaHttpHandler.sendResponse now validate the callback immediately upon extraction and, if invalid, short-circuit to a safe text/plain 400 response ("Invalid callback given") instead of ever entering the streaming/non-streaming dispatch — so no code path can wrap an unvalidated callback into an executable text/javascript response. Because the JVM agent's ParsedUri.getParameter() always returns the final decoded value regardless of whether the query string used a single "callback" param or a repeated/array param, this single validation point at the sink covers both parsing branches called out in the alert, as well as URL-encoded bypass variants (decoding happens before validation).
